entries.note: PMC5552472 full text read; quote is the abstract sentence. Ex vivo primary MDS marrow ADCC model dosed with BI 836858 itself. Untested opener correct; NCT02240706 started 2015-01-22, before the paper, as the draft says.

PMC9614517 full text: sentence verbatim incl. the 'BI 835858' typo; it is the authors' own model-vs-patient comparison (comparison_stated true). Engagement read as the PD readout (MDSC depletion, NK activation), as in cf-cftr; note the paper also says CD33 target engagement did occur. Registry results-first-posted 2020-12-21 confirmed.
PMID 23770776 abstract (Blood 2013;122:1455); quote verbatim. AML xenografts give a potency ranking, no exposure target; untested is right. Abstract-only, as the draft states.

NCT02706899 results: quote verbatim in the phase 1 primary-outcome description; results first posted 2018-12-21; why-stopped 'Sponsor decision based on portfolio prioritization'; 19 enrolled. 'No pharmacokinetic parameters were calculated' confirmed in Komrokji 2022.
PMID 11792178 abstract (Bioconjug Chem 2002;13:47); quote verbatim; nude-mouse HL-60 xenograft confirmed. Untested opener for the class is right; no MDS model existed.
Same PMC full text: quote is the abstract sentence; model is the n=10 MDS BM-MNC methylcellulose colony assay (CFU-GM, BFU-E). Second untested entry justified by the model change.

Quote verbatim but it compares PD data with clinical activity; the colony model is never named, and the same paragraph says no efficacy conclusion can be drawn (premature termination). Rules 1+4 give untested; set comparison_stated false, source_calls_it null; swap quote to the 'No conclusions on the efficacy' sentence.

Label PDF extracted: quote verbatim in 13.1; section 13 lists oval-cell hyperplasia and reproductive findings, nothing on sinusoidal injury or VOD, so 'silent' is accurate. Year 2000 vs print_year 2017 is a rule-6 opener, filing year inferred. Note cites 'Giles 2002': it is Giles 2001 (Cancer 92:406, DOI 10.1002/1097-0142(20010715)92:2<406::aid-cncr1336>3.0.co;2-u), cohort 92 AML + 25 advanced MDS.

Abstract (PMID 27683177, epub 2016-09-28, CCR 2017;23:1760) states the study was run to explain SOS already reported in patients: a reproduction, not a prediction. Not the model the class relied on (entry 1 is), surrogate non-binding conjugate PF-0259 (no class drug in model), patient side gemtuzumab AML and inotuzumab ALL (CD22, not this class). Not same; keep only as an untested model-change marker or drop; set model_filed false.

missing: safety: the patient side of gemtuzumab VOD does exist inside the MDS context: Giles 2001 (DOI 10.1002/1097-0142(20010715)92:2<406::aid-cncr1336>3.0.co;2-u) reports VOD in 14/119 patients, 25 of them advanced MDS. No source states the animal-tox-vs-patient comparison, so under rule 1 it supports only untested; under a silence-contra reading it would make the relied-upon rat/monkey tox model contra (2001), not same.

safety: the draft's own note names the 2016 FDA hepatotoxicity hold on vadastuximab and the CASCADE deaths but cites nothing; if a primary source (FDA hold letter, Fathi/Stein trial papers) states what the tox package predicted, that is the class's MDS-era safety comparison. Not searched here (budget).

dose: the cell opens in 2013 (vadastuximab xenografts) although gemtuzumab's monkey PK/tox (2000, same label source as safety entry 1) was the class's first dose model; status would still be untested, so low priority.

efficacy: Estey 2002 (gemtuzumab +/- IL-11 in AML/high-risk MDS) is named in the note as the class's MDS patient readout but is not cited or verified here; adding it would not change the status (no model comparison stated).
rule_questions: Efficacy 2022: the primary source reports 0/27 responses, says the sponsor stopped the trial for 'lack of single-agent efficacy (hematologic response)', and ties the null to the failed mode of action, yet explicitly states no efficacy conclusion can be drawn and never names the colony model. Is that contra (sponsor's stated reason) or untested (authors decline, comparison not stated)? I applied rules 1 and 4 and called it untested; the fact fields let it be re-scored.

Post-hoc models: a model built after the patient outcome was known (Guffroy 2017 monkey SOS) reproduces rather than predicts. The status table has no 'reproduced' state; same should require a prediction that preceded, or was at least independent of, the patient result. Proposed reading: untested (or exclude), never same.

Cross-indication evidence: does a model-vs-patient comparison made in AML or ALL patients count for an MDS context? The brief says validity belongs to the context, so I treated it as not counting unless the cohort includes MDS patients (Giles 2001 does; Guffroy's patient references do not).

Silence-contra sourcing: the safety question allows 'or its silence', but rule 1 needs a source that states the comparison. A label whose section 13 is silent while section 5.1 reports VOD is two statements in one document, not a stated comparison. The brief should say whether that counts (comparison_stated true/false) or whether a sentence like 'not predicted by nonclinical studies' is required.

Engagement means the PD readout, not binding: Komrokji says CD33 target engagement occurred but the predicted ADCC depletion and NK activation did not. Following the cf-cftr (sweat chloride) and ad-amyloid (plaque clearance) examples I kept contra; the brief could state this explicitly.
Opener year: safety entry 1 carries year 2000 (rule 6, first use) but print_year 2017 (house convention year = print_year); the two rules conflict for openers sourced from a later label.
